subject: physics
title: Momentum and conservation of momentum
key_idea: **Momentum** is mass × velocity. It is a property of every moving object, and it has a direction. In a closed system, the total momentum before an event equals the total momentum after it. This is **conservation of momentum**.

blocks.text: This section defines momentum and shows how to calculate it.

items.meaning: A property of a moving object. It depends on the mass and the velocity of the object.
Speed in a given direction, so momentum has a direction too.

blocks.label: Momentum
where: momentum, p, is in kilograms metre per second, kg m/s
mass, m, is in kilograms, kg
velocity, v, is in metres per second, m/s

items: A bigger mass at the same velocity has more momentum.
A greater velocity for the same mass gives more momentum.
Convert masses to kilograms first. For example, 180 g = 0.180 kg.

diagram.alt: Calculate the momentum of a moving skater.
diagram.question: A skater of mass {m} kg moves at {v} m/s. Calculate the momentum of the skater.

items: Momentum = mass × velocity, in kg m/s.
Momentum has a direction, the same as the velocity.
Convert grams to kilograms before you calculate.

blocks.text: In a closed system, no external forces act. The total momentum stays the same.

items.meaning: A group of objects with no forces acting from outside the group.
The total momentum before an event equals the total momentum after the event.

blocks.label: Conservation of momentum
blocks.formula: total momentum before = total momentum after

items: When two objects collide, momentum is transferred from one object to the other.
The momentum of one object decreases and the momentum of the other increases.
The total momentum does not change.
Objects with equal and opposite momentum before a collision have a total momentum of zero. If they stop in the collision, the total after is still zero.
Two objects at rest have a total momentum of zero.
When they push apart, one moves one way and the other moves the opposite way.
Their momenta are equal and opposite, so the total is still zero.
The total momentum before an event equals the total momentum after.
In a collision, the momentum of one object decreases and the other increases by the same amount.
Equal and opposite momenta add up to zero.

blocks.text: (Separate science) To find an unknown velocity, write total momentum before equals total momentum after.

items.text: Add the momentum of each object. Give a direction a sign: one way is positive, the opposite way is negative.
Write the total after in the same way. Use the unknown velocity.
Set total momentum before equal to total momentum after, then rearrange.
The direction of the answer matches its sign.

blocks.text: Skater A has a mass of 60 kg and moves at 3.0 m/s. She collides with skater B, mass 40 kg, who is at rest. They move off together.
Try the slider. Change the mass of each skater and the speed of skater A.

diagram.alt: Skater A collides with a stationary skater B and they move off together. Change the masses and the speed to see the velocity after the collision.

items: State that total momentum is conserved in the collision.
The momentum of one object increases, so the momentum of the other decreases.
Use momentum = mass × velocity. If the mass is constant, a change in momentum means a change in velocity.
Use trolleys on a runway, with light gates, data loggers or ticker timers to record the velocities.
Measure the mass of each trolley, and the velocities before and after the collision.
Calculate the total momentum before and after to check that they match.
Add up the momentum of every object, with signs for direction.
Set the total before equal to the total after, then rearrange for the unknown.
A negative sign for a velocity only shows the opposite direction.

checks.q: A trolley of mass 0.50 kg moves at 4.0 m/s. Calculate its momentum.
State what is meant by conservation of momentum.
checks.a: In a closed system, the total momentum before an event is equal to the total momentum after the event.

checks.q: A 2.0 kg trolley moving at 3.0 m/s hits a stationary 1.0 kg trolley. They stick together. Calculate their velocity.
checks.a: Momentum before = 2.0 × 3.0 = 6.0 kg m/s. 6.0 = (2.0 + 1.0) × v, so v = 2.0 m/s.

exam_phrases: (total) momentum is conserved in the collision
(total) momentum before collision = (total) momentum after collision
since momentum = mass × velocity, velocity (of train) decreases
the momentum of each car before the collision was equal (in magnitude) and opposite (in direction)
total momentum is zero after the collision
(total) momentum is shared between skater A and skater B

mistakes.wrong: Momentum is lost when skater A hits skater B, so skater A slows down.
mistakes.right: Momentum is conserved. The momentum of skater A decreases and the momentum of skater B increases, so the total before equals the total after.
Convert the mass first: 180 g = 0.180 kg. Then 0.216 = 0.180 × v, so v = 1.2 m/s.

mistakes.wrong: The bumper cars stop because they hit each other at the same speed.
mistakes.right: The momentum of each car before the collision was equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, so the total before was zero. Momentum is conserved, so the total after is zero.

worked_example.question:
A toy train collides with a stationary carriage on the track.

Explain why the velocity of the train after the collision is less than it was before the collision.

Use ideas about momentum in your answer.
answer_points: Total momentum is conserved in the collision.
During the collision the momentum of the carriage increases.
So the momentum of the train decreases.
Since momentum = mass × velocity, the velocity of the train decreases.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each linked step, ending with momentum = mass × velocity.

exam_phrases: transfer of momentum between Q and R

mistakes.right: Check the power of ten. 6.6 × 10⁻²⁶ × 480 = 3.2 × 10⁻²³ kg m/s. The right digits with a wrong power of ten score 2 marks.

mistakes.wrong: Momentum is lost in the collision.
mistakes.right: There is no overall change in momentum. Momentum is transferred between the two objects, so the change in momentum of one is equal and opposite to the change of the other.

mistakes.wrong: The forces are equal and opposite, so momentum is conserved.
mistakes.right: Link the steps. The forces are equal and opposite for the same time, so the changes in momentum are equal and opposite, so there is no overall change.

worked_example.question:
An atom of mass 6.6 × 10⁻²⁶ kg is moving with a velocity of 480 m / s.

Calculate the momentum of the atom.
worked_example.tip: One mark each for selecting the equation, substituting and evaluating. Any answer that rounds to 3.2 × 10⁻²³ scores the evaluation mark.

extra.heading: Explaining conservation with Newton's laws (Higher tier)

items: (Higher tier) In a collision, the force of R on Q is equal and opposite to the force of Q on R.
The time of the collision is the same for both objects.
So the change in momentum of Q is equal and opposite to the change in momentum of R.

mistakes.wrong: The skaters start at rest, so the momentum is zero and skater B does not move.
mistakes.right: The total before is zero, so the total after is zero. Skater B's momentum is equal and opposite to skater A's: 0 = (40 × 2) + 50 vB.

mistakes.wrong: Skater B has a velocity of −1.6 m/s, so I must have made a mistake.
mistakes.right: The sign only shows the opposite direction. The sign is ignored, so 1.6 m/s scores full marks.
Divide by the mass of skater B. 80 = 50 vB, so vB = 1.6 m/s.

worked_example.question:
Two skaters are standing, at rest, opposite each other on an ice rink.
Skater A has a mass of 40 kg and skater B has a mass of 50 kg.

Skater A pushes against skater B with a force of 30 N.

After pushing skater B, skater A has a velocity of 2 m / s.

Calculate the velocity of skater B after being pushed by skater A.
answer_points: 80 = 50 vB, using the momentum of skater A, 40 × 2 = 80 kg m/s.
worked_example.tip: A correct answer of 1.6 m/s scores 3 marks. Writing 0 = (40 × 2) + 50 vB is also allowed.
